classification.difficultyReason: Identify the smallest turn preserving each whole figure and count repetitions in a full turn; the open curve requires recognising a half-turn about its central midpoint.

content.prompt: State the order of rotational symmetry of each of the diagrams.

spec.description: Non-square tall rectangle with both diagonals, paired side ticks and bottom-left right-angle marker. Ordinary source-blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: Opposite vertical sides have single ticks; opposite horizontal sides have double ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: No rotational order or rotation annotations supplied.

answer.worked: The rectangle and its diagonals fit onto themselves after $180^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. The order is $360^\circ\div180^\circ=2$.

spec.description: Square with both diagonals, one equality tick on every side and a bottom-left right-angle marker. Ordinary source-blue strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: Four equal sides with a right angle establish a square.

answer.worked: The square and its diagonals fit onto themselves after $90^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $270^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. The order is $360^\circ\div90^\circ=4$.

spec.description: Six congruent narrow pointed petals, equally spaced, with one opposite pair vertical and a red common centre. Petal outlines use house black.
spec.mathematics: Six petals at angular intervals of 60 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No rotation arrows or order supplied.

answer.worked: A $60^\circ$ turn about the marked centre moves each petal onto the next. The order is $360^\circ\div60^\circ=6$.

spec.description: Continuous thick open curve, reconstructed geometrically rather than as a font glyph. A central vertical segment joins matching opposite semicircular bends; upper free end right and lower free end left. Source-blue silhouette uses house black.
spec.mathematics: Opposite semicircular bends and central segment have half-turn symmetry.
spec.answerVisibility: No centre or rotational order supplied.

answer.worked: A $180^\circ$ turn about the midpoint of the central segment interchanges the two bends and makes the curve fit onto itself. The order is $360^\circ\div180^\circ=2$.
